about: Overworld food webs for chiacraft: species by tier, a web per biome, and ecological rules of thumb. See 'Overworld food webs.md'. 'est.' marks this report's own estimates; 'ref.' standard natural history not checked this session.

webs.place: Kansas tallgrass prairie (Konza Prairie, Flint Hills)

trees: gallery oak and hackberry along streams

webs.notes: Konza stocks bison at 1 animal unit per 4.7 ha to remove 25% of growth; wolves gone from Kansas by ~1900, keep rare; dung beetles and rot are the decomposers.

webs.place: Temperate deciduous forest (Bialowieza, Poland; eastern US variant)
webs.notes: The capybara's forest habitat (gallery forest) has no jaguar in this web; the wolf stands in. Wolves killed 72 red deer, 31 boar and 16 roe /100 km2/yr at 2.3 wolves/100 km2, limiting but not regulating deer. Ungulates 65-1,180 kg/km2. US variant: white-tailed deer, wild turkey, coyote, black bear, turkey vulture.

webs.place: Hemiboreal birch forest (southern Finland, Moscow region)
webs.notes: The moose is the big browser here (later); until then deer and boar carry the role. Raccoon dogs share the fox's niche.
Hares cycle (~10 yr): 14.7 to 0.2 per ha in one Kluane decline; lynx kill 0.3-1.2 hares/day. Wood bison is the cow's role in Canada. Moose, lynx, bear, beaver later.
Lemmings cycle every 3-5 years and drive Arctic fox breeding; a snowy owl eats ~1,600 a year. A High Arctic web is mostly top-down. Neither chihuahua nor cat lives here.

Two growing seasons (winter rains, July-Sept monsoon). Kangaroo rats never drink; kit foxes and wildcats barely do: water should be optional for desert species. Coyotes cause over 75% of kit fox predation.

grass: Hymenachne and Leersia in the flooded lows

webs.notes: Wet May-Oct, dry Nov-Apr. Capybaras 10/km2 (Guarico) to 200-350/km2 peaks (Apure); dry season packs capybaras, caimans and waders at shrinking pools. Caracara and vultures take newborn capybaras; the harpy eagle is not a llanos bird.

Floods Dec-May. Ranch cattle (31.7% of jaguar kills in the southern Pantanal) are the player's cows here, not wild prey. Taiama jaguars: caiman in 55% of scats, fish 46%, mammals 11%; 12.4 jaguars per 100 km2. Rising water spreads caimans and raises jaguar kills of them. Capybaras 3.2-14.8/km2.
Alpine marmot (golden eagle's main prey) as a rodent until it exists. Rockies: elk, bighorn, mountain goat, pika, puma, wolverine, grizzly.

webs.place: Temperate coast, open water (North Sea / North Atlantic)
webs.notes: Phytoplankton does most of the production. Aquatic herbivores eat ~51% of primary production, three times land herbivores.

water_plants: wrack and kelp on the strandline

webs.notes: The tide line is the beach's carrion: gulls, crabs, ravens and foxes clean it.

predator_prey_biomass.text: 10,000 kg of prey supports ~90 kg of a given carnivore species (~111 kg prey per kg carnivore), whatever its size; carnivore number per prey biomass scales as 1/mass

prey_size_switch.text: carnivores under 21.5 kg take mostly prey under half their mass (incl. invertebrates); larger ones take prey near their own mass; invertebrate intake rates are ~1/10 of vertebrate feeders'

small_hunter_max_prey.text: largest usual prey of a small hunter as a share of its mass

pack_max_prey.text: design value from ECOLOGY.md; real wolf packs take 4-10x one wolf's mass (ref.)

trophic_transfer.text: ~10% of energy passes up a level (Lindeman 1942; his data 0.1-37.5%); marine 2-24%, mean ~10%

herbivory_share_of_growth.text: share of yearly plant production eaten by herbivores
herbivory_share_of_growth.source: Cyr & Pace 1993; Konza bison fact sheet

livestock_vs_wild_biomass.text: livestock reach ~10x wild herbivore biomass for the same productivity; herbivore biomass, consumption and production all rise with primary production

herbivore_biomass_rain.text: large herbivore biomass rises with rainfall in African reserves

water_l_day.text: mammal drinking water; carnivores and desert animals get much of it from food

base:plains.text: managed bison 1 AU per 4.7 ha removing 25% of growth (~100 kg/ha); wild est. 10-30 kg/ha

base:savanna.text: capybara 10/km2 (Guarico) to 200-350/km2 peaks (Apure); flood meadow optimum 1.6-3/ha

base:taiga.text: hares 0.2-15/ha through the cycle; moose and caribou est. 0.1-2/km2

base:snowy_plains.text: est. caribou 0.1-1/km2 year-averaged, herds of thousands on migration; lemmings 1-100+/ha in cycle

base:desert.text: est. 1-5 kg/ha; mule deer 0.5-2/km2; kangaroo rats 5-50/ha

base:mountains.text: est. chamois and ibex 2-10/km2 on summer pastures

wolf_yellowstone.value: 1.9 elk per wolf per month in winter (1.6 early, 2.2 late)

wolf_bialowieza.value: 72 red deer, 31 boar, 16 roe /100 km2/yr at 2.3 wolves/100 km2 (~50 ungulates/wolf/yr, est.)

lynx_bialowieza.value: 110-169 roe /100 km2/yr at 2.4-3.2 lynx (~1 roe per 7 days, est.); 21-36% of spring roe

predation_share_of_prey_per_year.text: one predator's yearly take of a prey population
predation_share_of_prey_per_year.source: Okarma et al. 1997; Jedrzejewski et al. 2002

lago_guri.value: rodents, howlers, iguanas, leaf-cutter ants 10-100x mainland density on predator-free islands; saplings severely reduced

st_matthew.value: 29 reindeer (1944) to ~6,000 (1963) to 42 (1966); lichen 1 cm vs 8-12 cm

bialowieza.value: wolves limited but did not regulate deer; predation was inversely density dependent

checks_for_the_game.overshoot_model: reduced regrowth then starvation, not unlimited growth
